name: Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN)
issuer: the Ministry of Customs and Revenue
note: Samoa's sheet (its government's own sheet on the OECD's automatic-exchange portal ('Information on Tax Identification Numbers'; the OECD's index page sits behind a bot check and wasn't opened, the sheet itself came straight back)), read 2026-10-30: TINs are governed by sections 12 to 14 of the Tax Administration Act 2012; a TIN is issued when a person engaged in business obtains a business licence (on approval of the application) or employs people, and is not issued automatically to tax residents; it is used for income tax, VAGST and PAYE. There is no structure: numbers are issued in sequence (from 70004; the sheet's example runs 11001, 11002). The length isn't stated: the format reads the sheet's five-digit numbers. Read as given on application (the business licence), to anyone; needed for tax. Samoa's national digital identity, if any, isn't read here. No check rule, age, fee or time is stated.

sources.title: OECD AEOI portal, Samoa: Information on Tax Identification Numbers (the jurisdiction's own sheet)
sources.said: TINs are governed by sections 12 – 14 of the Tax Administration Act 2012. ... The TIN is issued upon approval of the business license application. ... There is currently no specific or unique structure for the digits allocated for each TIN. ... Issuance of TIN started from the number 70004, there is also no specific reason for why it started from this number. ... If by today the TINs issued has come up to the number 11001, the next person who will register for a TIN will receive the TIN number of 11002.
